questions.question: In how many categories are loans provided under the MUDRA loan scheme?
questions.solution:

questions.question: Which of the following is a selective credit instrument?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Credit rationing**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Credit rationing** is a selective credit instrument used by central banks to control the amount of credit that is available to the economy.
 
• This tool is used to ensure that credit is directed towards essential sectors and activities, thereby influencing the allocation of resources in the economy.
 
• Unlike tools like the Bank Rate or CRR, which affect the overall credit conditions in the economy, credit rationing specifically targets certain sectors or types of credit.
 
• This method can be particularly useful during times of economic stress or when certain sectors are deemed to be of strategic importance.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Variable reserve ratio** refers to the changing reserve requirements that banks must hold, which influences their ability to lend money.
 
• **Bank rate** is the rate at which the central bank lends money to commercial banks, influencing the overall level of interest rates in the economy.
 
• **CRR (Cash Reserve Ratio)** is the percentage of a bank's total deposits that must be maintained with the central bank in the form of liquid cash.
 
• Selective credit control measures like credit rationing are part of the broader monetary policy toolkit used by central banks to achieve economic stability and growth.

questions.question: Which of the following forces can only be applied when in contact with an object?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Frictional force**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Frictional force** is a contact force that acts between two surfaces in contact with each other.
 
• It resists the relative motion or tendency of such motion of two surfaces in contact.
 
• This force is only present when there is physical contact between the objects.
 
• Other forces like gravitational, electrostatic, and magnetic can act at a distance without direct contact.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Gravitational force** is a non-contact force that acts between two masses over a distance.
 
• **Electrostatic force** is a non-contact force that acts between charged particles over a distance.
 
• **Magnetic force** is a non-contact force that acts between magnetic poles or currents over a distance.
 
• Contact forces like friction require physical interaction between objects, while non-contact forces can act through space without direct physical contact.

questions.question: In which year were four new Directive Principles added to the original list?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1976**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **1976** is the year when four new Directive Principles were added to the original list.
 
• The **42nd Amendment Act** of 1976 is responsible for this addition.
 
• The new principles included in the amendment were focused on **securing participation of workers in the management of industries, promoting equal justice and free legal aid, protection of environment and wildlife, and promotion of international peace and security.**
 
• The Directive Principles of State Policy aim to create social and economic conditions under which the citizens can lead a good life.
 
• They also direct the state to ensure distributive justice and to promote the welfare of the people by securing a social order in which justice, social, economic, and political, shall inform all the institutions of national life.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Directive Principles of State Policy** are enumerated in **Part IV** of the Constitution of India from Articles 36 to 51.
 
• They are guidelines for the framing of laws by the government. These provisions are not enforceable by any court, but the principles laid down therein are considered fundamental in the governance of the country.
 
• The idea of such policies has been borrowed from the **Irish Constitution**.
 
• The principles aim to establish social and economic democracy in the country.
 
• Although non-justiciable, the Directive Principles have been used to interpret the scope and ambit of Fundamental Rights in various landmark judgments.

questions.question: Which of the following Governor-Generals of British India was in favour of free press and repealed the press regulations of 1823?

• **Lord Metcalfe** was the Governor-General of British India who was in favour of a free press.

• Lord Metcalfe's repeal of these regulations was a landmark event in the history of the Indian press, allowing for greater freedom of expression and the growth of journalism in India.
 
• His actions were praised by many contemporary Indian and British journalists and intellectuals.

questions.question: How many types of makeup (vesham) are used for the performers of Kathakali dance?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**5 types**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **5 types** of makeup (vesham) are used for the performers of Kathakali dance.
 
• The five types of vesham are **Pacha (green), Kathi (knife), Thadi (beard), Kari (black), and Minukku (radiant).**
 
• Each type of vesham represents a particular character type, ranging from noble heroes to villainous characters, sages, and divine beings.
 
• The makeup is elaborate and symbolic, involving intricate facial paintings and headgear that help in portraying the character's nature and role in the performance.
 
• The colors and designs in the makeup are not arbitrary; they follow a traditional code that has been passed down through generations of Kathakali artists.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Kathakali** is a classical Indian dance-drama known for its colorful makeup, elaborate costumes, and expressive gestures.
 
• It originated in the state of **Kerala** in the 17th century and combines elements of dance, drama, and music to tell stories from Hindu epics like the Mahabharata and Ramayana.
 
• The performers undergo rigorous training, which includes mastery in facial expressions, body movements, and the ability to convey emotions through their eyes and gestures.
 
• The dance form is traditionally performed as an all-night event, starting in the evening and continuing until dawn.
 
• Kathakali has gained international recognition and is performed worldwide as a symbol of India's rich cultural heritage.

questions.question: Epilimnetic, metalimnetic, and hypolimnetic water strata are example of:

options.text: typical thermal stratification of a lake

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**typical thermal stratification of a lake**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Epilimnetic, metalimnetic, and hypolimnetic water strata** are characteristic layers in the thermal stratification of a lake.
 
• In a stratified lake, the **epilimnion** is the uppermost layer where the water is warm and well-mixed.
 
• The **metalimnion** (or thermocline) is the middle layer where temperature changes rapidly with depth.
 
• The **hypolimnion** is the deepest layer, consisting of cooler, denser water that is typically more stable and less mixed.
 
• This stratification is crucial for understanding lake ecology, including temperature distribution, oxygen levels, and nutrient cycling.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The process of stratification typically occurs in temperate regions during the summer when the surface water is heated by the sun.
 
• During the fall, the surface water cools, and the entire lake can mix in a process called **turnover**, which helps distribute oxygen and nutrients throughout the lake.
 
• Understanding these layers helps in managing lake ecosystems, particularly in relation to fisheries, water quality, and habitat conservation.
 
• Human activities such as pollution and water extraction can disrupt natural stratification, leading to ecological imbalances.

questions.question:
Which of the following statements are correct regarding the jurisdiction of the Supreme Court of India?

A. Original jurisdiction extends to any dispute between the Government of India and one or more States or between the Government of India and any State or States on one side and one or more States on the other or between two or more States.

B. Appellate Jurisdiction extends when the Union plus some States are one side and some other States on the other side of the dispute.

C. Under Articles 129 and 142 of the Constitution, the Supreme Court has been vested with the power to punish for contempt of court.

D. As of now, the International Commercial Arbitration cannot be initiated in the Supreme Court.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**3) A and C only**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Original Jurisdiction:** Statement A is correct. The Supreme Court's original jurisdiction extends to any dispute between the Government of India and one or more States or between the Government of India and any State or States on one side and one or more States on the other or between two or more States.
 
• **Contempt of Court:** Statement C is also correct. Under Articles 129 and 142 of the Constitution, the Supreme Court has been vested with the power to punish for contempt of court.
 
• Statement B is incorrect because the appellate jurisdiction does not extend to disputes where the Union and some States are on one side and other States are on the other side.
 
• Statement D is incorrect as the Supreme Court can entertain international commercial arbitration matters under its jurisdiction.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Supreme Court of India is the highest judicial forum and final court of appeal under the Constitution of India.
 
• It has extensive powers in the form of original, appellate, and advisory jurisdictions.
 
• The Supreme Court's decisions are binding on all other courts within the territory of India.
 
• The Supreme Court can also transfer cases from one High Court to another and even from one subordinate court to another in the interest of justice.

questions.question: Abolition of titles is mentioned in which Article of the Indian Constitution?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 18**__

__
 
• **Article 18** of the Indian Constitution deals with the abolition of titles.
 
• It states that no title, not being a military or academic distinction, shall be conferred by the State.
 
• The Article aims to prevent the creation of a class of nobility and uphold the principle of equality among citizens.
 
• This provision ensures that the state does not recognize or grant any titles that could create social hierarchies.

• It lays down the framework defining fundamental **political principles, establishes the structure, procedures, powers, and duties of government institutions**, and sets out fundamental rights, directive principles, and the duties of citizens.
 
• The Constitution of India is the **longest written **constitution of any country in the world.
 
• It declares India a **sovereign, socialist, secular, and democratic republic, assuring its citizens justice, equality, and liberty, and endeavors to promote fraternity.**
 
• The **Seventh Schedule **of the Constitution contains three lists which delineate the subjects under the **Union, State, and Concurrent lists**.
 
• Amendments to the Constitution can be made through a process outlined in **Article 368**.
 
• The Union List has been amended several times to meet the evolving needs of the nation.

questions.question: In which amongst the following acts was Delhi declared the capital of British India in place of Calcutta?

• **Morley - Minto Act, 1909** declared Delhi as the capital of British India, replacing Calcutta.
 
• This act is also known as the **Indian Councils Act 1909**.

• The shift was officially implemented in 1912.
 
• The move aimed to have a more centrally located capital and to placate the growing political unrest in Bengal.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Government of India Act, 1858** marked the end of the East India Company's rule in India and transferred control to the British Crown.
 
• The **Government of India Act, 1935** provided for provincial autonomy and the establishment of a federal government in India.
 
• The **Montagu Chelmsford Act, 1919**, also known as the Government of India Act 1919, introduced a dual system of governance (dyarchy) in the provinces.
 
• Delhi was chosen for its strategic location and historical significance as a seat of power in India.
 
• The shift of the capital was a significant event in the history of British India, symbolizing administrative and political changes.

• Nor'Westers are part of the larger weather patterns affecting the Indian subcontinent during the hot weather season.

• Unlike a fixed resistor, a rheostat allows for the manual adjustment of resistance to control current flow.
 
• Common applications include light dimmers, motor speed controllers, and adjusting the volume of audio devices.
 
• Rheostats are typically constructed with a resistive wire wound around an insulating ceramic core, with a sliding contact that moves along the wire.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• An **Ammeter** is used to measure the current in a circuit.
 
• A **Conductor** allows the flow of electric current with minimal resistance.
 
• A **Voltmeter** is used to measure the voltage across two points in a circuit.
 
• Rheostats are often used in educational settings for experiments and demonstrations involving Ohm's law and other electrical principles.
 
• They are crucial components in circuits where variable resistance is required for tuning or calibration purposes.

questions.question: Which of the following rivers is joined by the Chambal River from the south?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Yamuna**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Chambal River joins the Yamuna River from the south.
 
• Chambal is one of the major tributaries of the Yamuna River.
 
• The Chambal River originates in the Vindhya Range just south of Mhow in western Madhya Pradesh.
 
• It flows in a northerly direction through Madhya Pradesh before turning southeast to form the boundary between Rajasthan and Madhya Pradesh, and then between Rajasthan and Uttar Pradesh.
 
• Eventually, it merges with the Yamuna River in Uttar Pradesh.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Yamuna is the longest and the second-largest tributary river of the Ganges (Ganga) in northern India.
 
• It originates from the Yamunotri Glacier at a height of about 6,387 meters on the southwestern slopes of Banderpooch peaks in the Lower Himalayas in Uttarakhand.
 
• Yamuna traverses several states including Uttarakhand, Haryana, Uttar Pradesh, and Delhi.
 
• Key cities along the Yamuna include Delhi, Agra, and Mathura.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/a2ee087f9fb8a2870685960f103a0b6bc92eb3b7edf99a801c4004a14ad807cf.png]

questions.question: According to the Global Hunger Index 2022, what is the rank of the neighbouring country, Bangladesh out of 121 countries?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**84th**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Bangladesh** is ranked **84th** out of 121 countries in the Global Hunger Index 2022.
 
• The Global Hunger Index (GHI) is a tool designed to comprehensively measure and track hunger at global, regional, and national levels.
 
• The GHI scores countries on a 100-point scale, where 0 is the best possible score (no hunger) and 100 is the worst.
 
• The index is calculated based on four key indicators: undernourishment, child stunting, child wasting, and child mortality.
 
• Countries with higher GHI scores are experiencing higher levels of hunger and undernutrition.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Global Hunger Index** is published annually by Concern Worldwide and Welthungerhilfe.
 
• The 2022 report highlights that progress in combating hunger has been uneven across regions and countries.
 
• Many countries with the highest levels of hunger have been affected by conflict, climate change, and economic shocks.
 
• Efforts to combat hunger must be multifaceted, involving improvements in food security, nutrition, health, and education.
 
• The Global Hunger Index aims to raise awareness and understanding of regional and country differences in hunger and to trigger actions to reduce hunger around the world.

questions.question: Good Friday is related to:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Christians**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Good Friday is a significant day for **Christians** worldwide.
 
• It commemorates the crucifixion of **Jesus Christ** and his death at Calvary.
 
• Good Friday is observed during **Holy Week** as part of the Paschal Triduum on the Friday preceding Easter Sunday.
 
• The day is marked by various traditions including fasting, prayer, and church services.
 
• It is a solemn day reflecting on the sacrifice of **Jesus Christ** for humanity's sins.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Good Friday is also known as **Holy Friday, Great Friday,** and **Black Friday**.
 
• Many Christian denominations, including **Catholics, Protestants, and Eastern Orthodox**, observe this day with various rituals and customs.
 
• The date of Good Friday varies each year as it is based on the **lunar calendar** and the ecclesiastical approximation of the March equinox.
 
• In some countries, Good Friday is a public holiday, allowing people to attend religious services and spend time in reflection and prayer.
 
• The significance of Good Friday lies in its reminder of the ultimate sacrifice and love of **Jesus Christ**, which is central to Christian faith.
